key_insight: Matching data across zeroth-order finite-difference evaluations cancels oracle noise, while mismatched on-policy evaluations amplify it as 1/μ².
engineering_relevance: ZO-BOLT offers a route to memory-efficient LLM post-training by applying zeroth-order optimization to an RLVR-aligned weighted-SFT objective.
method: Analyze gradient-estimation variance under matched versus mismatched evaluation data.
Derive convergence guarantees with explicit constants separating the two regimes.
Apply zeroth-order optimization to Boltzmann Targeted SFT (BOLT).
evidence_signal: Perturbation-scale sweeps and matched-versus-mismatched comparisons support the theory; tests across three model variants and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over pretrained baselines with near-inference memory use.
watch_item: Reliable implementation requires preserving data matching across paired evaluations; the abstract does not establish generalization beyond the tested models and math benchmarks.
paper_title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning
